- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) and forecast is high, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.3) and forecast is low, raise forecast slightly to avoid underreaction.  
- If recent price history shows a sharp spike followed by a steep drop, reduce forecast for next period by 10–15% to account for mean reversion.  
- If forecast is consistently above true outcome over 3–5 periods, apply a downward bias correction of 2–5% per period.  
- If sentiment is volatile or mixed (±0.3–0.6), avoid large directional moves; use smoother, trend-following adjustments.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome deviates > 3% from 10-day moving average, adjust forecast to align with recent mean.  
- If sentiment history shows a recent reversal (e.g., from +1.0 to -0.3), reduce forecast momentum and apply a lagged correction.
